Description: Stable Windows Update optional-content and Delivery Optimization policies plus a choice-aware Windows Settings preference
Purpose: Keep optional non-security updates user-selected, leave early continuous-innovation rollout off unless the user already selected it in Windows Settings, preserve the user's Microsoft-product update preference, and disable peer-to-peer delivery

1_OptionalUpdatesPolicy.Name: Let users select optional updates

SetAllowOptionalContent.Description: Official AllowOptionalContent policy mapping: users select which optional updates to receive; no automatic optional preview/CFR enrollment

1_OptionalUpdatesPolicy.GUIPath: Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Optional updates (managed policy)

2_ContinuousInnovationPreference.Name: Do not prioritize early non-security and feature updates

IsContinuousInnovationOptedIn.Description: Windows Settings preference with the early continuous-innovation rollout toggle off; regular security updates are unaffected

2_ContinuousInnovationPreference.GUIPath: Settings > Windows Update > Get the latest updates as soon as they're available

3_DeliveryOptimization.Name: Downloads from other devices (DISABLED for privacy)

DODownloadMode.Description: 0 = HTTP only (Microsoft servers), no P2P, no LAN sharing

3_DeliveryOptimization.GUIPath: Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Delivery Optimization > Allow downloads from other devices = OFF

MSBestPractice: Both policy values are mapped to current Microsoft documentation; the raw Windows Settings UX preference is written only when no stamped manual opt-in is active. Regular security updates remain enabled, while forced schedules, deadlines and restart policies are not configured
UserControl: Optional non-security updates remain user-selected; a stored manual early-rollout opt-in is preserved and reported NotChecked; the existing Microsoft-product update preference is preserved; restart scheduling remains Windows-managed
NoInteractivePrompt: No mode selection needed - stable optional-update behavior and HTTP-only delivery are the fixed hardening contract
CRITICAL_NOTE: The official AllowOptionalContent Group Policy mapping writes only SetAllowOptionalContent. Value 3 keeps optional updates user-selected, whereas value 1 automatically installs optional cumulative updates and CFRs; per Microsoft's policy matrix value 3 deliberately delegates the early-rollout decision to the Settings toggle. IsContinuousInnovationOptedIn=0 is a raw Windows Settings UX preference, not a documented managed policy. When the toggle is on, Windows stores a stamped opt-in intent (CIOptinModified) and the Update Session Orchestrator re-commits 1 over a direct raw write at boot and on Settings/USO activity. NoID Privacy therefore preserves an active stamped user opt-in, reports exactly that value NotChecked, excludes it from SettingsApplied, and instructs the user to turn the toggle off in Settings to select the hardened state; value 1 without the intent stamp remains a failure. NoID Privacy deliberately does not write AllowMUUpdateService because changing update-source enrollment can trigger downstream product updates that BAVR cannot uninstall. SetAllowOptionalContent and DODownloadMode policy CSPs document Pro/Enterprise/Education/IoT Enterprise, not Home, so Home has only the choice-aware continuous-innovation UX target. DODownloadMode=0 disables peer-to-peer caching but retains HTTP/CDN downloads.
